summary: Karl Brugmann worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied under Georg Curtius around 1870–1871 and succeeded him in 1885. Brugmann held posts at the University of Freiburg (~1884–1887) and Leipzig University (~1887–1919).

Karl Brunnhölzl works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He studied under traditional teachers Khenpo Tsültrim Gyamtso Rinpoche, Tenga Rinpoche, Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche, Sangye Nyenpa Rinpoche, Ringu Tulku, and Lama Thubten, and teachers Lambert Schmithausen and Klaus-Dieter Mathes.

Karl Debreczeny specializes in Tibetology and history and archaeology. He completed his PhD at the University of Chicago (~2001–2007) under doctoral supervisor Wu Hung and teacher Jenny Purtle, later serving as curator at the Rubin Museum of Art around 2007.

Karl Ferdinand Johansson was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Uppsala University in 1880 and served there as University Professor of Sanskrit and the Comparative Philology of the Indo-European Languages from around 1893 to 1925.

Karl Florenz worked in Japanology, Indology, and linguistics. After studying at the University of Göttingen (~1885–1887), he served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1889–1914) and held a post at the University of Hamburg (~1914–1934).

Karl Friedrich Geldner worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Tübingen and Leipzig under Rudolf von Roth, Hermann Brockhaus, and Ernst Windisch, holding posts at Tübingen, Halle-Wittenberg, Berlin, and Marburg.

Karl H. Potter worked in Indology and philosophy, having studied at Harvard University in 1955. He held professorships at the University of Minnesota (~1956–1970) and the University of Washington (~1970–1997).

Karl Hoffmann was a scholar in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Saarland University (~1952–1955) and served as a professor at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1955–1983).

Karl Jettmar was a scholar of history, archaeology, Indology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He held posts at Johannes Gutenberg University Mainz (~1961–1964) and served as professor at Heidelberg University (~1964–1983).

Karl Richard Lepsius worked in linguistics, history, and archaeology. He studied at Leipzig, Göttingen, and Berlin, later holding posts at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1846–1884) and serving as Chief Librarian at Berlin State Library (~1873–1884).

Karl Rosenkranz was a philosopher who studied at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1824–1826), Heidelberg University (~1826–1827), and University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1827–1828). He later held a post at the University of Halle-Wittenberg (~1830–1833).
Karl Verner worked in linguistics. He studied at Aarhus Katedralskole from around 1857 to 1864 and held a post at the University of Copenhagen from around 1883 to 1896.

Karl-Heinz Brodbeck works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. After studying at LMU Munich (~1970–1976), he held posts at Ifo Institute (~1977–1982), LMU Munich (~1982–1991), and became professor at FHWS and Munich School of Politics in 1992.
Karl-Heinz Everding is a Tibetologist. He held the post of PD Dr. at the University of Bonn and served as PD Dr. at the University of Hamburg in 2005.

Karma Lekshe Tsomo works in Buddhist and religious studies, earning a doctorate at University of Hawaii (~1993–2000). She held posts at Chaminade University, East-West Center, University of San Diego (~2000), and UC San Diego.

Karma Phuntsho works in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1997–2003) under Michael Aris and David Seyfort Ruegg, and held a post-doctoral position at the CNRS (~2003–2004).

Karma Sonam Palmo works in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology. She completed degrees at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and earned a PhD at the University of Tasmania (~2011–2017) supervised by Lucy Tatman and Sonam Thakchoe.

Karma Ura works in Tibetology and other fields. He completed undergraduate studies at Magdalen College, Oxford (~1980–1983) and a graduate degree at the University of Edinburgh (~1983–1984), becoming Director of the Centre for Bhutan Studies around 1999.

Karuna Kusalasaya worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. He was a research scholar and Assistant to the Director at Visva-Bharati University (~1939–1944) and later served as Professor of Sanskrit at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University.

Karunesh Shukla is a scholar in Indology and Buddhist studies. He served as Professor and Head of the Department of Sanskrit and Prakrit Languages at Deen Dayal Upadhyaya Gorakhpur University and founded the Nagarjuna Buddhist Foundation.
